articles.title: Vectorized CLZ and CTZ
articles.summary: Vectorized CLZ and CTZ are instructions that compute the number of leading (trailing) zero bits in a fixed-size integer, with CLZ being the easier of the two. The general idea involves substituting a 32-bit number into the mantissa of a floating-point exponent to get a double representing 2k(1 + 2 - 52x), then subtracting 2k as a double to get 2k - 52x. This trick can be used to compute clz, and it also implements clz for completeness. The implementation of clz is efficient, with a latency of 0.45 ns per iteration on a Haswell CPU, but it can be optimized further.
